title: A marvelous work
summary: The Lord declares that He will do a marvelous work, remember His covenants and promises, recover His people, and send forth the words of Nephi’s seed.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord says He will do a marvelous work, remember His covenants, and recover His people, who are of the house of Israel.
The Lord says He will remember promises to Nephi and his father and that the words of Nephi’s seed will go forth to his seed and to the ends of the earth.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Represent the divine speech as off-screen narration; no visible divine appearance is described.
unspecified_visual_details: Any visible speaker, setting, appearance, or physical objects.

narration.text: there shall be many—at that day when I shall proceed to do a marvelous work among them
my words shall hiss forth unto the ends of the earth, for a standard unto my people

doctrinal_or_story_notes: These are prophetic declarations, not events shown occurring in the present.
prohibited_inventions: Depicting a future recovery or gathering as already happening.
Showing the Lord visibly; no appearance is described.

title: A Bible—and no more?
summary: The Lord foretells that many Gentiles will say they have a Bible and that there cannot be any more Bible.

explicit_facts.text: Many Gentiles will say they have a Bible and there cannot be any more Bible.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Render the Gentiles’ words as off-screen speech over an unspecified setting.
unspecified_visual_details: The identity, appearance, number, and setting of the Gentiles.

narration.text: many of the Gentiles shall say: A Bible! A Bible!
We have got a Bible, and there cannot be any more Bible.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The statement is presented as a future saying, not a narrated present-time gathering.
prohibited_inventions: A specific group or historical setting for the Gentiles.

title: The Bible from the Jews
summary: The Lord says the Bible will proceed from the Jews, His ancient covenant people, and challenges the Gentiles to remember their labor and diligence.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord says the Bible proceeds from the Jews, His ancient covenant people, and asks what thanks the Gentiles give them.
The Lord asks whether the Gentiles remember the Jews’ travails, labors, pains, and diligence in bringing salvation to the Gentiles.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Present the questions as off-screen divine narration; the Jews and Gentiles need not be pictured.
unspecified_visual_details: Any people, place, manuscripts, or depicted historical labor.

narration.text: it shall proceed forth from the Jews, mine ancient covenant people.
And what thank they the Jews for the Bible which they receive from them?

doctrinal_or_story_notes: This is divine teaching and rhetorical questioning, not a narrated scene of historical events.
prohibited_inventions: Showing the Jews’ historical labor as a present event.
Inventing visual details for the ancient covenant people.

title: The Lord has not forgotten
summary: The Lord rebukes the Gentiles for cursing and hating the Jews and for claiming no more Bible is needed; He declares that He has not forgotten His people.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord says the Gentiles have cursed and hated the Jews and have not sought to recover them; He will return these things upon their own heads and has not forgotten His people.
The Lord challenges the person who says they have a Bible and need no more to consider whether they obtained it except by the Jews.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Use off-screen divine speech rather than depicting a specific audience.
unspecified_visual_details: The physical identity or appearance of the addressee and any setting.

narration.text: I the Lord have not forgotten my people.
Have ye obtained a Bible save it were by the Jews?

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The promised return of consequences is not depicted as occurring now.
prohibited_inventions: A visible punishment or a present-time confrontation.

title: More nations than one
summary: The Lord teaches that He created all people, remembers those on the isles of the sea, rules in heaven and earth, and brings His word to all nations.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord says He created all people, remembers those on the isles of the sea, rules in heaven and earth, and brings His word to all nations.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Present the teaching as off-screen narration; the verse does not describe a visible divine appearance.
unspecified_visual_details: Specific nations, islands, people, and geography.

narration.text: Know ye not that there are more nations than one?
I, the Lord your God, have created all men
I bring forth my word unto the children of men, yea, even upon all the nations of the earth?

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verse teaches the Lord’s rule and care; it does not narrate a visible tour of the world.
prohibited_inventions: Literal depiction of the Lord in the heavens or on earth.

title: Two nations’ testimony
summary: The Lord asks why people murmur at receiving more of His word and teaches that testimony from two nations will witness that He is God and remembers each nation.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord says the testimony of two nations witnesses that He is God and remembers one nation like another; their testimonies will run together.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Use off-screen narration and avoid literalizing the figure of testimonies running together.
unspecified_visual_details: The nations and any physical representation of their testimony.

narration.text: the testimony of two nations is a witness unto you that I am God
when the two nations shall run together the testimony of the two nations shall run together also.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: “Run together” describes testimony, not a literal visual event.
prohibited_inventions: Literal merging of nations or documents.

title: The work is not finished
summary: The Lord says He is the same forever, may speak another word, and that the Bible need not contain all His words because He has caused more to be written.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord says He is the same yesterday, today, and forever, speaks according to His pleasure, and His work is not finished.
The Lord says the Bible need not contain all His words and that He has caused more to be written.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Treat the statements as off-screen narration rather than visualizing time or the unfinished work.
unspecified_visual_details: Any visible speaker, book, writing, or setting.

narration.text: I am the same yesterday, today, and forever;
my work is not yet finished;
ye have a Bible ye need not suppose that it contains all my words;

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The claims are teachings and declarations, not a depiction of a particular act of writing.
prohibited_inventions: A visible divine figure or invented writing event.

title: Words written among the nations
summary: The Lord commands people in all regions to write His words and says He will speak to the Jews, Nephites, other tribes of Israel, and all nations, who will write them.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord commands people in all directions and on the islands of the sea to write His words; the books will be used in judgment according to works and what is written.
The Lord says He will speak to the Jews, Nephites, other tribes of Israel, and all nations, and they shall write it.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Use off-screen speech over an unspecified setting; the future writing is not shown as occurring.
unspecified_visual_details: The writers, their locations, scripts, books, and writing implements.

narration.text: I command all men, both in the east and in the west, and in the north, and in the south
they shall write the words which I speak unto them;
I shall also speak unto all nations of the earth and they shall write it.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: These are prophecies and commands, not a montage of present-time writing scenes.
prohibited_inventions: Depicting unmentioned individuals writing or appearing as present characters.

title: Words exchanged
summary: The Lord foretells that the Jews, Nephites, and lost tribes of Israel will have one another’s words.

explicit_facts.text: The Jews and Nephites will have one another’s words; both will have the words of the lost tribes, and the lost tribes will have the words of the Jews and Nephites.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Render as off-screen narration; do not visualize the exchange literally.
unspecified_visual_details: How the words are transmitted, their form, and the locations or appearance of the peoples.

narration.text: the Jews shall have the words of the Nephites
the lost tribes of Israel shall have the words of the Nephites and the Jews.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The exchange is a future promise, not a present event.
prohibited_inventions: Inventing a meeting or physical exchange of books.

title: Gathered home
summary: The Lord foretells that the house of Israel will be gathered to its lands of possession, His word will be gathered in one, and He will show those who fight His word and people that He is God and remembers His covenant with Abraham.

explicit_facts.text: The house of Israel will be gathered home to its lands of possession, and the Lord’s word will be gathered in one.
The Lord will show those fighting His word and people that He is God and covenanted with Abraham to remember his seed forever.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Keep the declaration as off-screen narration; the gathering and showing are future and not depicted as occurring.
unspecified_visual_details: The lands, gathered people, opponents, and manner of showing.

narration.text: my people, which are of the house of Israel, shall be gathered home unto the lands of their possessions;
I covenanted with Abraham that I would remember his seed forever.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The passage is prophetic and contains no narrated present-time gathering or confrontation.
prohibited_inventions: Depicting future gathering or conflict as a current event.
